title: vgi-rpc access log record
description: Cross-language conformance schema for one record on the vgi_rpc.access logger. See docs/access-log-spec.md for the full prose.

protocol_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical __describe__ payload.

trace_id.description: W3C trace ID of the span this call ran under, 32 lowercase hex characters. Present when the server participates in a trace; absent otherwise. This is the join key between an access-log record and the surrounding distributed trace -- request_id only correlates within one service.

span_id.description: W3C span ID for this call, 16 lowercase hex characters. Present whenever trace_id is; the two are emitted together or not at all.

request_bytes.description: On-wire size of the request body as received, before decompression. This is what the peer actually sent -- distinct from input_bytes, which measures logical Arrow buffers after decoding. Use this for egress/ingress accounting.

response_bytes.description: On-wire size of the response body as sent, after compression. Distinct from output_bytes, which measures logical Arrow buffers and is routinely orders of magnitude larger. Absent when the size cannot be known (a streamed response with no content length).

externalized_bytes.description: Bytes uploaded to external storage during this call. These never appear in the HTTP body -- only a pointer batch does -- so they are invisible to transport-level accounting and are frequently the largest of the three byte figures. Absent when nothing was externalised.

truncated.description: Set when the record does not carry everything it otherwise would. true = the formatter shed fields to fit a per-record size cap. "record_too_large" = the sentinel form, where most optional fields were dropped. "payload_omitted" = nothing was lost to a cap; the emitter is simply not logging request payloads at this level. Consumers looking for real data loss MUST distinguish "payload_omitted" from the other two, since it is the common case on a normally-configured server.

sample_rate.description: Fraction of successful calls the emitting server was keeping when this record was written. Present only when sampling is active (a rate below 1). A consumer counting calls from a sampled log MUST divide by it. Errors are never sampled, so error records may be absent this field even when sampling is on.

original_request_bytes.description: Length in characters of the request_data field that was dropped due to truncation.

session_id.description: Sticky session ID (12-byte hex, 24 chars). Present when the request was bound to a sticky session — i.e. carried a VGI-Session header that resolved to a live registry entry, or the method called ctx.open_session/close_session.

session_action.description: Lifecycle action for the sticky session this request touched. 'open' = ctx.open_session was called; 'resume' = a valid VGI-Session token resolved to a live entry and dispatch ran; 'close' = ctx.close_session was called; 'none' (or absent) = the request did not interact with sticky machinery. Middleware-short-circuit cases (token validation failed; entry aged out) currently do not produce access-log records — they short-circuit before dispatch.

dropped_records.description: Records lost to a full async queue since the last successful enqueue. Present on the first record through after a drop.

allOf.description: method_type=unary requires request_data unless the record was truncated
Call statistics: all six fields present together or all absent
